1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane
Root-owned construction, ordinary proofs, complete instruments and costs.

RESULT AND STATUS
=================

The strongest construction in this continuation is a finite-duration,
finite-strength parity measurement whose entire intended output field carries
only Z1 Z2. It uses three finite harmonic modes, two ordinary reciprocal
beam-splitter couplings, one dispersive qubit-mode coupling, and two actual
longitudinal qubit-mode drives. All auxiliary modes return to vacuum at the
end of the same operation. No stationary spectral approximation, eliminated
receiver, infinitely fast feedback, or unobserved final apparatus is used.

For vacuum initial auxiliaries and vacuum reservoirs, the controlled coherent
state dilation is exact at every finite drive strength within this Hamiltonian
model. It proves preservation of arbitrary superpositions within BOTH parity
sectors, not only correct reported parity or equality of basis-state outlet
marginals. Finite detection efficiency affects assignment, but does not by
itself leak within-parity information through the main output.

Intrinsic auxiliary losses are retained exactly. Their unobserved part gives
an explicit error functional. Accessible losses can instead be corrected from
their photon records with only local Pauli/Z rotations. Their no-click rates
are independent of the logical state. The full binned measurement instrument
is composed into a CNOT with nonzero helper, local-gate and readout errors.

This is a mathematically complete operation in a stated effective model. It
is NOT a demonstrated lower-resource fault-tolerant computer or a validated
hardware proposal. Ordinary optimized control improves its first waveform.
Thermal auxiliary populations and noncommuting data faults expose important
remaining errors. No hardware advantage, new threshold, or historical
priority is established. The architecture changes an inherited operational
consequence; the mission-level cost advantage remains open.

input-independent mixture of an ideal gauge check and a localized faulty

EXACT FINITE-MEDIATOR EXPOSURE LAW AND THE INFORMED CONTROL COMPARISON
1 November 2026. Root owns the apparatus construction. This memo derives
its unavoidable intrinsic-loss exposure and optimizes its physical pulses.

1. Declared model and the scope of the result

The actual three oscillator modes are b,c,m. The Hamiltonian is

 H = g[(b^dag+c^dag)m + m^dag(b+c)] + chi Z1 c^dag c
     + u(t) Z2(b+b^dag) + w(t) Z2(c+c^dag).

The vacuum outlets are sqrt(Gamma)m, sqrt(kb)b, sqrt(kc)c. Parameters g,chi
are nonzero and time independent. The physical forces u,w are real. Data
Z1,Z2 are conserved throughout this derivation. Modes start in vacuum and
must return to vacuum at T. No eliminated mediator or chiral channel is
assumed. Write P=Z1 Z2, h=Gamma/2, ab=kb/2, ac=kc/2.

Root's exact all-time parity-output family is

 b = U P + i B Z2,       c = V P - i B Z2,
 m = i A P/sqrt(Gamma),

with real amplitudes and

 A = sqrt(Gamma)(U'+ab U)/g,
 V = -(A'+h A)/(g sqrt(Gamma))-U,
 B = [g A/sqrt(Gamma)-V'-ac V]/chi,
 u = -B'-ab B,          w = B'+ac B-chi V.            (1)

A smooth compact U with sufficiently many zero endpoint derivatives
constructs the full experiment. With U=sin^6(pi t/T) times any finite cosine
polynomial, U through U^(5) vanish at the endpoints. A,V,B and both drives
therefore start and end at zero. This also handles known kb,kc exactly.

Within the stated Hamiltonian and real-force class, (1) is necessary for
an exactly parity-only main outlet, not just a lucky ansatz. Branch fields
lie in the span of P and Z2 because the drives create Z2 and dispersion
multiplies c by Z1. Requiring no Z2 component of m at all times forces the
Z2 components of b,c to be opposite. The b equation forces its Z2 component
to be purely imaginary; the c equation then forces its P component to be
real and the m equation its P component to be imaginary. Their real
coefficients obey exactly (1). A broader actuator class, non-vacuum input,
an approximate output condition, or a different covariance changes this
necessity statement.

2. Exact intrinsic-loss functional

Inside a fixed P sector, the b,c fields for the two different Z2 values
differ by +2iB and -2iB. The inaccessible independent vacuum outputs thus
give, after allowed deterministic local Z1 phase correction,

 V_sector = exp[-2(kb+kc) I_B],       I_B=int_0^T B(t)^2 dt,
 p_Z = [1-exp(-2(kb+kc)I_B)]/2.

Write a=kb/2=kc/2>=0. The actual b equation gives

 A=(sqrt(Gamma)/g)(U'+aU).

Multiplying by exp(at), integrating, and using U(0)=U(T)=0 gives
 int_0^T exp(at)A(t)dt=0 exactly. This is a weighted zero-area condition,
not an assertion that A has zero unweighted mean.

Exact mode reset gives A=0 because m=0, and A'=0 because b+c=0 in the
m equation. The construction is smooth enough that these endpoint traces
exist. Define f=exp[a(t-T/2)]A. Then f=f'=0 at both endpoints and int f=0.
Moreover,

 A''=exp[-a(t-T/2)](D-a)^2f,
 exp[-2a(t-T/2)] lies in [exp(-aT),exp(aT)].

Thus the direction of the weighted inequality is

 ||A''||^2/||A||^2 >= exp(-2aT) ||(D-a)^2f||^2/||f||^2.       (1)

Expand the numerator. The odd cross terms integrate to endpoint terms
in f^2 and (f')^2 and vanish. The remaining cross term is
2a^2 int f'' f = -2a^2||f'||^2, which combines with the +4a^2||f'||^2
from (-2af')^2. Consequently, with the signs and coefficients retained,

 ||(D-a)^2f||^2=||f''||^2+2a^2||f'||^2+a^4||f||^2.             (2)

The sharp clamped, zero-mean derivative inequality is
 ||f''||^2 >= (beta2/T)^4||f||^2, beta2=7.853204624095838.
It is not inferred by identifying zero mean with orthogonality to the
